title.narrative: Co-guarantee with Proparco and Equity BCDC in DRC
Garanti med Proparco och Equity BCDC i DRK

description.narrative:
Insatsen är en låneportföljgaranti från Sida och AFD/Proparco som syftar till att främja tillgången till finansiering för mikroföretag och små och medelstora företag (MSME) i Demokratiska Republiken Kongo, med fokus på hälsosektorn, utbildning, start-up och sektorn för förnybar energi, som bidrar till landets ekonomiska tillväxt.
Insatsen faller under Strategin för Sveriges utvecklingssamarbete med Demokratiska republiken Kongo, 2021-2025, resultatområden (1) Mänskliga rättigheter, demokrati, rättsstatens principer och jämställdhet, (2) Jämlik hälsa, och (3) Miljö, klimat och hållbart nyttjande av naturresurser

This contribution is a Sida and AFD/Proparco loan portfolio guarantee intended to promote access to finance for Micro Small and Medium sized enterprises (MSME) in the Democratic Republic of the Congo, with focus on the health, education, start-up and renewable energy sector contributing to the economic growth of the country.
The intervention falls under the Strategy for Sweden’s development cooperation with Democratic Republic of the Congo, 2021-2025. The result areas relevant for this contribution are: (1) Democracy, Human Rights, Rule of Law, Gender Equality; (2) Health Equity; and (3) Environment, climate, sustainable use of natural resources.

No results in terms of loans granted for 2024. The year 2024 was primarily dedicated to training EQUITY BCDC agents on the provisions of the Convention and the "Pegasse/Proparco" management system. This enabled agents to better understand how to use the guarantee and the reporting system.
This is the third agreement signed with the same Equity BCDC bank, this time in collaboration with PROPARCO, focusing on the health and energy sectors.
We launched the Co-Guarantee with the AIDS team, which includes Albert Granholm and Camilla Rubensson, both program officers at GARANALYS, as well as Charlotte Mukadi, program officer at the embassy, and the PROPARCO delegation. This launch focused on training client advisors, loan officers, credit analysts, and administrative staff. Forty participants, including members of management and representatives from provincial agencies who participated online, were also present. The main topics covered included the insurance structure, client eligibility criteria and other important conditions, the claims and compensation application process, and the PROPACO reporting system. Participants showed great interest, and many questions were answered.
It was an excellent start, as it allowed the guarantee officers to better understand the terms of the guarantee and learn how to report within the system. These concepts are essential for the proper use of the Guarantee. The discussions also helped to reduce stereotypes about financing in the health and energy sectors, which are relatively new areas for banking.
The discussions helped to alleviate some of the stereotypes associated with financing in the health and energy sectors. Credit analyses indicated that they refrain from managing all loans related to these different sectors. For some, these are complex loans, while others were unaware before the training that these areas could be handled by the bank.
The head of the Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises (MSME) department concluded the session by emphasizing the importance of guarantees and urging staff to review all applications without exception. The credit committee determines whether a loan should be included in the guarantee portfolio. We greatly appreciated this training, particularly the enriching discussions. We hope it will help the team achieve significant results by 2025: an increase in the percentage of guaranteed loans
